items.title: The local P1 Crouzeix–Raviart element
items.statement:
Let $d\ge2$ and let $K$ be a nondegenerate affine $d$-simplex with vertices
$a_0,\ldots,a_d$ and facets $F_i$ opposite $a_i$. Write
$\lambda_0,\ldots,\lambda_d$ for its barycentric coordinate functions, so
$\lambda_i(a_j)=\delta_{ij}$ and $\sum_i\lambda_i=1$. The local
Crouzeix–Raviart polynomial space is $\mathbb P_1(K)$, the real affine
functions on $K$. Its face-average functionals are
$$\sigma_{K,F_i}(p):=\frac1{|F_i|}\int_{F_i}p\,dS,\qquad p\in\mathbb P_1(K).$$
The candidate dual shape polynomial associated with $F_i$ is
$$\phi_{K,F_i}:=1-d\lambda_i.$$
The next item proves that these $d+1$ functionals are unisolvent and that the
displayed polynomials form their dual basis. No pointwise continuity across
different cells is part of this local element.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: §§36.2.1–36.2.2, PDF pp. 2–4: local affine polynomial space and face-average degrees of freedom.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
references.locator: §25.2, lines 276–290: the nonconforming P1 triangle and the midpoint/face degrees of freedom.

items.title: Fractional Sobolev regularity on a simplex
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded open set,
$0<r<1$, and let $q$ be a measurable real function on $U$. Define
$$[q]_{H^r(U)}^2:=\int_U\int_U\frac{|q(x)-q(y)|^2}{|x-y|^{d+2r}}\,dx\,dy,$$
with the diagonal integrand set to zero, and
$H^r(U):=\{q\in L^2(U):[q]_{H^r(U)}<\infty\}$, using almost-everywhere
classes and norm $\|q\|_{H^r(U)}^2:=\|q\|_{L^2(U)}^2+[q]_{H^r(U)}^2$.
For $u\in H^1(U)$, write $u\in H^{1+r}(U)$ when each weak derivative
$\partial_j u$ belongs to $H^r(U)$, and define
$$|u|_{H^{1+r}(U)}^2:=\sum_{j=1}^d[\partial_j u]_{H^r(U)}^2.$$
For vector fields, use the sum of the componentwise squared $H^r$ norms.
Use these definitions on each cell $K$ and on the full domain $\Omega$, with
$\|u\|_{H^{1+r}(U)}^2:=\|u\|_{H^1(U)}^2+|u|_{H^{1+r}(U)}^2$. At $r=1$,
set $H^1(U)=W^{1,2}(U)$, interpret $[q]_{H^1(U)}^2:=\|\nabla q\|_{L^2(U)}^2$,
and set $H^{1+r}(U)=W^{2,2}(U)$ with the ordinary integer-order norm and
membership of [[def-sobolev-space-wkp-and-its-norm]]. Thus
$|u|_{H^2(U)}^2=\sum_{j,k}\|\partial_k\partial_j u\|_{L^2(U)}^2$. The local
seminorm is the restriction of the Slobodeckij convention in
[[def-fractional-slobodeckij-space-on-euclidean-space]] to $U\times U$.

references.locator: Lemma 36.1, PDF p. 2, and Lemma 36.8, PDF pp. 6–7: W^{1+r,2} and face traces for r>1/2.

items.title: A Poincare bound on a slab-bounded domain
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be open and satisfy
$a<x\cdot e<b$ for a unit vector $e$ and all $x\in\Omega$, with $a<b$.
Then every $v\in H^1_0(\Omega)$ satisfies
$$\|v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le(b-a)\|\nabla v\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$
The argument assumes Countable Choice through the stated Sobolev,
product-measure, and affine change-of-variables interfaces; it does not use the
Axiom of Choice.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Chapter 3, Traces and Poincare inequalities
references.locator: §3.3, Lemma 3.27, printed p. 32: zero-boundary Poincare–Steklov inequality; Exercise 3.2, printed p. 35: the one-dimensional fundamental-theorem argument.

references.title: Richard S. Laugesen, Linear Analysis and Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 3
references.locator: §3.10, Theorems 3.17–3.18 and their proofs, printed pp. 64–66.

items.title: Face averages are unisolvent for the local Crouzeix–Raviart element
items.statement:
For the element of [[def-crouzeix-raviart-local-p1-element]], the face-average
functionals form an isomorphism
$\mathbb P_1(K)\to\mathbb R^{d+1}$. In particular,
$$\frac1{|F_j|}\int_{F_j}\phi_{K,F_i}\,dS=\delta_{ij},\qquad \phi_{K,F_i}=1-d\lambda_i,$$
so every $p\in\mathbb P_1(K)$ has the unique expansion
$p=\sum_{i=0}^d\sigma_{K,F_i}(p)\phi_{K,F_i}$.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: §36.2.1, equations (36.4)–(36.5) and the shape functions on PDF p. 2.

references.locator: §25.2, lines 276–290: the affine P1 space is specified by face-midpoint values in two dimensions.

items.title: The global homogeneous Crouzeix–Raviart space
items.statement:
Let $\Omega\subset\mathbb R^d$ be a bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral
domain with a finite matching affine simplicial mesh $\mathcal T$. Here
Lipschitz polyhedral means that the boundary is a finite union of flat
simplex faces and, near each boundary point after a rigid coordinate change,
$\Omega$ lies on one side of a Lipschitz graph. Let $\mathcal F^\circ$ and
$\mathcal F^\partial$ be its interior and boundary facets. For a cellwise
affine function $v$, write $v_K$ for its polynomial restriction to $K$. The
broken gradient $\nabla_hv$ is defined by $(\nabla_hv)|_K:=\nabla v_K$.
For a facet $F$ and an integrable function $w$ on $F$, let $h_F:=\operatorname{diam}(F)$ and write $\operatorname{avg}_F(w):=|F|^{-1}\int_Fw\,dS$.
The homogeneous Crouzeix–Raviart space is
$$V_h^{CR,0}:=\left\{v\in L^2(\Omega): v_K\in\mathbb P_1(K)\ \text{for each }K\in\mathcal T,\quad \int_F(v_{K^+}-v_{K^-})\,dS=0\ \text{for }F=K^+\cap K^-\in\mathcal F^\circ,\quad \int_Fv_K\,dS=0\ \text{for }F\in\mathcal F^\partial\right\}.$$
The ordering $K^+,K^-$ on an interior facet is arbitrary; the zero-mean
condition is independent of that ordering. The functions need not agree
pointwise on a facet and need not belong to $H^1(\Omega)$.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: §36.2.2, equation (36.7) and the homogeneous boundary subspace (36.8), PDF pp. 3–4.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
references.locator: §25.2, lines 280–290: piecewise P1 functions whose face means agree.

items.title: Fractional face traces and cellwise Green identity on a simplex
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $K$ be a shape-regular affine $d$-simplex,
$F\subset\partial K$ a facet, and $1/2<r\le1$. Every $q\in H^r(K)$ has a
single-valued $L^2(F)$ trace $\gamma_Fq$. For $1/2<r<1$,
$$\|\gamma_Fq\|_{L^2(F)} \le C\left(h_K^{-1/2}\|q\|_{L^2(K)} +h_K^{r-1/2}[q]_{H^r(K)}\right),$$
and
$$\|\gamma_Fq-\operatorname{avg}_F\gamma_Fq\|_{L^2(F)} \le C h_K^{r-1/2}[q]_{H^r(K)},$$
while for $r=1$,
$$\|\gamma_Fq\|_{L^2(F)} \le C\left(h_K^{-1/2}\|q\|_{L^2(K)} +h_K^{1/2}\|\nabla q\|_{L^2(K)}\right),$$
and the face-mean fluctuation is bounded by
$C h_K^{1/2}\|\nabla q\|_{L^2(K)}$.
The constant depends only on $d$, the shape-regularity bound, and $r$.

If $u\in H^1(K)$, $\nabla u\in H^r(K;\mathbb R^d)$, and
$f=-\Delta u\in L^2(K)$ distributionally, then for every $w\in H^1(K)$,
$$\int_Kfw\,dx=\int_K\nabla u\cdot\nabla w\,dx -\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\int_F(\gamma_F\nabla u\cdot n_{K,F})\gamma_Fw\,dS.$$
Here $n_{K,F}$ is the outward unit normal. The trace threshold $r>1/2$ is
used to make the normal-gradient trace an $L^2$ function.

The two cell traces of a global $H^1(\Omega)$ function agree on a shared
interior facet, and the trace of a global $H^1_0(\Omega)$ function vanishes
on a boundary facet. More generally, if $1/2<r<1$ and $q\in H^r(\Omega)$,
then its two traces on each shared interior facet agree almost everywhere.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: Lemma 36.8 and its proof, PDF p. 6: face-mean Poincare estimate for H^s, s>1/2; Lemma 36.10, PDF pp. 9–10: cellwise Green identity and consistency.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
references.locator: §25.2, lines 314–343: elementwise integration by parts and subtraction of face means in the H2 case.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is used through the declared integration, density, and approximation suppliers; no Axiom of Choice is invoked.

items.title: A Dirichlet Poisson smoothing index
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded domain and let $1/2<s\le1$. Say that $\Omega$ has
a **Dirichlet Poisson smoothing index $s$** with constant $C_{\rm reg}$ if,
for every $g\in L^2(\Omega)$, there is a unique $\zeta_g\in H^1_0(\Omega)$
satisfying
$$\int_\Omega\nabla\zeta_g\cdot\nabla v\,dx =\int_\Omega g v\,dx\qquad(v\in H^1_0(\Omega)),$$
and $\zeta_g\in H^{1+s}(\Omega)$ with
$$\|\zeta_g\|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)}\le C_{\rm reg}\|g\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$
This is a hypothesis about the continuous adjoint Poisson problem. It is not
asserted for every bounded domain.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: §36.3.2, PDF pp. 11–13: the elliptic regularity index s in (1/2,1] and its L2 estimate.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is declared through the exact weak-solution and Sobolev interfaces; the smoothing property remains a domain hypothesis, and no Axiom of Choice is invoked.

items.title: Interior face means form the global Crouzeix–Raviart degrees of freedom
items.statement:
For every interior facet $F$, define $\phi_F$ to equal $\phi_{K,F}$ on each
cell $K$ incident to $F$ and zero on all other cells, where
$\phi_{K,F}$ is the local shape polynomial of
[[def-crouzeix-raviart-local-p1-element]]. Then
$\{\phi_F:F\in\mathcal F^\circ\}$ is a basis of the space in
[[def-crouzeix-raviart-global-space]]. The face mean $\bar v_F:=|F|^{-1}\int_F
v_K\,dS$ is single-valued for $v\in V_h^{CR,0}$ and
$\dim V_h^{CR,0}=|\mathcal F^\circ|$.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: Proposition 36.2 and its proof, PDF p. 3; the homogeneous restriction is described on PDF p. 4.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
references.locator: §25.2, lines 280–290: one face degree of freedom is shared by the adjacent cells.

items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used by this definition or finite-dimensional calculation.

items.title: The face-average Crouzeix–Raviart interpolant
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For $u\in H^1(K)$, use the facet traces of
[[lem-crouzeix-raviart-simplex-traces-and-green-identity]] and define its local
face-average interpolant by
$$I_K^{CR}u:=\sum_{F\subset\partial K}\left(\frac1{|F|}\int_Fu\,dS\right)\phi_{K,F},$$
where $\phi_{K,F}$ is the explicit polynomial in
[[def-crouzeix-raviart-local-p1-element]]. On a finite matching mesh, define
$I_h^{CR}u$ cellwise by $(I_h^{CR}u)|_K=I_K^{CR}(u|_K)$. For a global
$u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$, the cell traces agree on interior facets and vanish on
boundary facets, so this formula has the intended global Crouzeix–Raviart
degrees of freedom. The local estimate item proves its fractional
approximation bounds.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: §36.2.1, equations (36.4)–(36.6), and the global interpolation definition after Proposition 36.2, PDF pp. 2–4.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
references.locator: §25.2, lines 308–313: interpolation into the conforming P1 subspace used for approximation.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is assumed through the local simplex trace interface; no Axiom of Choice is invoked.

items.title: Face jumps are controlled by the broken gradient
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. For every matching shape-regular simplicial mesh and
$v_h\in V_h^{CR,0}$,
$$\sum_{F\in\mathcal F^\circ\cup\mathcal F^\partial} h_F^{-1}\|[v_h]_F\|_{L^2(F)}^2 \le C\|\nabla_hv_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}^2.$$
On an interior facet, $[v_h]_F=v_{K^+}-v_{K^-}$; on a boundary facet,
$[v_h]_F=v_K$. The constant depends only on $d$ and the shape-regularity
bound.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: Lemma 36.9, equations (36.14) and its proof, PDF pp. 7–8.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
references.locator: §25.2, lines 314–343: face-mean cancellation and local scaling of nonconforming jumps.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is required by the affine shape-scaling interface; no Axiom of Choice is invoked.

items.title: The Crouzeix–Raviart method for the homogeneous Poisson problem
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ and $\mathcal T$ be as in
[[def-crouzeix-raviart-global-space]], let $V:=H^1_0(\Omega)$, let
$V_h:=V_h^{CR,0}$, and let $f\in L^2(\Omega)$. The exact Poisson form and
load are
$$a(u,v):=\int_\Omega\nabla u\cdot\nabla v\,dx,\qquad F(v):=\int_\Omega f v\,dx\quad (u,v\in V).$$
An exact solution is a $u\in V$ satisfying $a(u,v)=F(v)$ for every $v\in V$.
For $v_h,w_h\in V_h$, define the broken form and discrete load by
$$a_h(v_h,w_h):=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K\nabla v_h\cdot\nabla w_h\,dx, \qquad F_h(w_h):=\int_\Omega f w_h\,dx.$$
The discrete problem is to find $u_h\in V_h$ such that
$a_h(u_h,w_h)=F_h(w_h)$ for every $w_h\in V_h$.

Put $X_h:=V+V_h$. For each cell facet $F\subset\partial K$, let
$\gamma_{F,K}$ denote the trace supplied by
[[lem-crouzeix-raviart-simplex-traces-and-green-identity]].
For $z\in X_h$ and $w_h\in V_h$, define the comparison-space extension
$$\widetilde a_h(z,w_h):=\sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\int_K \nabla(z|_K)\cdot\nabla w_h\,dx.$$
Each restriction $z|_K$ belongs to $H^1(K)$, and this extension agrees with
$a_h$ when $z\in V_h$.

On an interior facet
$F=K^+\cap K^-$ choose either ordering and define
$[z]_F:=\gamma_{F,K^+}z-\gamma_{F,K^-}z$; on a boundary facet of $K$ set
$[z]_F:=\gamma_{F,K}z$. The mesh-dependent comparison expression is
$$\|z\|_{\sharp,h}^2:= \sum_{K\in\mathcal T}\|\nabla(z|_K)\|_{L^2(K)}^2+ \sum_{F\in\mathcal F^\circ\cup\mathcal F^\partial} h_F^{-1}\|[z]_F\|_{L^2(F)}^2,\qquad z\in X_h.$$
The next items prove the required definiteness, stability, and consistency
properties; this definition makes no assertion that $V_h\subset V$.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
references.locator: §25.2, lines 247–315: second Strang setting, CR space, broken form, and consistency.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is declared through the local trace/Green and Sobolev interfaces; no Axiom of Choice is invoked.

items.title: The broken gradient is a norm on the homogeneous Crouzeix–Raviart space
items.statement:
For a finite matching mesh of a bounded connected polyhedral domain,
$v_h\mapsto\|\nabla_hv_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$ is a norm on
$V_h^{CR,0}$ of [[def-crouzeix-raviart-global-space]].

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: Lemma 36.4, PDF p. 4: the broken-gradient seminorm is a norm under the face-average boundary conditions.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
references.locator: §25.2, lines 282–290: the homogeneous nonconforming P1 space and broken-gradient norm.

items.axiom_use: No choice principle is used by this definition or finite-dimensional calculation.

items.title: Local approximation by the face-average Crouzeix–Raviart interpolant
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice and the setup of [[def-crouzeix-raviart-face-average-interpolant]], a
shape-regular affine mesh, and $1/2<r\le1$. The face-average interpolant is
defined for every $u\in H^{1+r}(K)$ by the traces of
[[lem-crouzeix-raviart-simplex-traces-and-green-identity]] and reproduces
$\mathbb P_1(K)$. Uniformly over all cells,
$$\|\nabla(u-I_K^{CR}u)\|_{L^2(K)} \le C h_K^r|u|_{H^{1+r}(K)},\qquad \|u-I_K^{CR}u\|_{L^2(K)} \le C h_K^{1+r}|u|_{H^{1+r}(K)}.$$
For each facet $F\subset\partial K$,
$$h_F^{-1/2}\|\gamma_F(u-I_K^{CR}u)\|_{L^2(F)} \le C h_K^r|u|_{H^{1+r}(K)}.$$
If $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$, then the global interpolant has matching interior
face means and zero boundary face means, so $I_h^{CR}u\in V_h^{CR,0}$.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: Lemma 36.1 and its proof, PDF p. 2: local interpolation estimate for every r in [0,1].

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
references.locator: §25.2, lines 326–343: reference-simplex Bramble–Hilbert interpolation estimate and face scaling in the H2 case.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is used through the local trace, reference Poincare, and affine shape-scaling suppliers; no Axiom of Choice is invoked.

items.title: A conforming averaging companion for Crouzeix–Raviart functions
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be the bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral domain and
$\mathcal T_h$ a finite matching shape-regular simplicial mesh of
[[def-crouzeix-raviart-global-space]]. For every $v_h\in V_h^{CR,0}$ there is
a continuous piecewise affine function $E_hv_h$ with zero boundary trace
such that
$$\|\nabla E_hv_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \le C\|\nabla_hv_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)},\qquad \|v_h-E_hv_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)} \le C h\|\nabla_hv_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)},$$
where $h=\max_{K\in\mathcal T_h}h_K$. In particular,
$E_hv_h\in H^1_0(\Omega)$.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: Lemma 36.9, PDF pp. 7–8: local averaging and jump control for CR functions.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
references.locator: §25.2, lines 280–350: the CR space, broken norm, and conformity defect.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is used through affine shape scaling, simplex Gauss–Green, measure continuity, and density suppliers; no Axiom of Choice is invoked.

items.title: The broken comparison expression is a norm
items.statement:
In the Poisson setting of [[def-crouzeix-raviart-poisson-method]],
$\|\cdot\|_{\sharp,h}$ is a norm on $X_h=H^1_0(\Omega)+V_h^{CR,0}$.
Its restriction to $H^1_0(\Omega)$ is the gradient norm, equivalent to the
$H^1$ norm, and its restriction to $V_h^{CR,0}$ is a norm.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: Lemma 36.4, PDF p. 4, and Lemma 36.9, PDF pp. 7–8: broken-gradient norm and scaled facet-jump estimate for the homogeneous CR space.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
references.locator: §25.2, lines 280–290: homogeneous CR face conditions and the broken-gradient norm.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice enters through the reference-simplex Poincare supplier; no Axiom of Choice is invoked.

items.title: Well-posedness of the homogeneous Poisson and CR problems
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice, let $\Omega$ and $\mathcal T_h$ be as in
[[def-crouzeix-raviart-poisson-method]], and let $f\in L^2(\Omega)$. The
exact weak problem has a unique solution $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)$, and the
discrete problem has a unique solution $u_h\in V_h^{CR,0}$. The exact
existence argument uses Countable Choice through Hilbert-space structure and
Lax–Milgram. The finite-dimensional discrete existence and uniqueness
argument uses no choice principle.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: §36.2.3, equations (36.9)–(36.11), PDF pp. 4–5: exact and discrete Poisson variational problems.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
references.locator: §25.2, lines 247–315: exact and discrete variational formulations and stability.

items.axiom_use: The exact Hilbert-space solve uses Countable Choice through Hilbert structure and Lax–Milgram. The finite face-basis matrix proof of the discrete solve uses no choice principle.

items.title: Discrete Poincare inequality for homogeneous Crouzeix–Raviart functions
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $\Omega$ be a bounded connected Lipschitz polyhedral domain and
$\mathcal T_h$ any finite matching shape-regular simplicial mesh. There is a
constant $C$ depending only on $\Omega$, $d$, and the shape-regularity bound
such that every $v_h\in V_h^{CR,0}$ satisfies
$$\|v_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C\|\nabla_hv_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: Lemma 36.6 and its proof, PDF pp. 5–6: the discrete Poincare–Steklov inequality, proved there by elliptic duality and face estimates.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
references.locator: §25.2, lines 280–312: the homogeneous CR space, broken-gradient norm, and conforming P1 subspace used for approximation.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is inherited through the conforming companion and continuous Poincare interfaces; no Axiom of Choice is invoked.

items.title: Consistency bounds for the Crouzeix–Raviart Poisson method
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $1/2<r\le1$, let $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)\cap H^{1+r}(\Omega)$ solve
$-\Delta u=f\in L^2(\Omega)$ distributionally, and let $h$ be the maximum
cell diameter of a finite matching shape-regular mesh. With the method of
[[def-crouzeix-raviart-poisson-method]], define
$$\mathcal R_h(u;v_h):=\widetilde a_h(u,v_h)-F_h(v_h),\qquad v_h\in V_h^{CR,0},$$
where $\widetilde a_h$ is the cellwise extension in [[def-crouzeix-raviart-poisson-method]]. Then
$$|\mathcal R_h(u;v_h)|\le C h^r|u|_{H^{1+r}(\Omega)} \|\nabla_hv_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}.$$
If also $1/2<s\le1$ and $\zeta\in H^1_0(\Omega)\cap H^{1+s}(\Omega)$,
then
$$|\mathcal R_h(u;I_h^{CR}\zeta)|\le C h^{r+s} |u|_{H^{1+r}(\Omega)}|\zeta|_{H^{1+s}(\Omega)}.$$
The constants depend only on $d$, the shape-regularity bound, $r$, and $s$.

items.title: Energy error estimate for the Crouzeix–Raviart Poisson method
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice. Let $1/2<r\le1$, and let $u\in H^1_0(\Omega)\cap
H^{1+r}(\Omega)$ solve $-\Delta u=f\in L^2(\Omega)$ on a bounded connected
Lipschitz polyhedral domain. On any finite matching shape-regular mesh, the
solution $u_h$ of the Crouzeix–Raviart method satisfies
$$\|u-u_h\|_{\sharp,h}\le C h^r|u|_{H^{1+r}(\Omega)}.$$
In particular, $\|\nabla_h(u-u_h)\|_{L^2(\Omega)}$ obeys the same bound.
The constant is independent of the mesh size and may depend on $\Omega$, $d$,
the shape-regularity bound, and $r$.

references.title: Jean-Luc Guermond, MATH 661 Fall 2025, Part VIII, Chapter 36, Crouzeix–Raviart approximation
references.locator: Theorem 36.11 and proof, PDF pp. 10–11: second-Strang application and the CR energy estimate.

references.title: Joachim Schöberl, Numerical Methods for Partial Differential Equations, Chapter 25, Non-conforming Finite Element Methods
references.locator: §25.2, lines 247–350: second Strang framework, CR interpolation, and H2 energy error proof.

items.axiom_use: Countable Choice is required by the imported nonconforming Strang theorem and exact Hilbert-space solve; no Axiom of Choice is invoked.

items.title: L2 error estimate under a Dirichlet Poisson smoothing index
items.statement:
Assume the hypotheses of the energy estimate with $1/2<r\le1$, and suppose
the domain has Dirichlet Poisson smoothing index $s$ with $1/2<s\le1$ and
constant $C_{\rm reg}$. Then
$$\|u-u_h\|_{L^2(\Omega)}\le C C_{\rm reg}h^{r+s} |u|_{H^{1+r}(\Omega)}.$$
The constant $C$ depends only on $d$, the mesh shape-regularity bound, $r$,
and $s$. No smoothing index is asserted for every bounded domain.

items.title: A zero-boundary solution below the CR trace regularity threshold
items.statement:
Every $u\in H^1_0((0,1)^2)$ belongs to $H^{1+r}((0,1)^2)$ for some
$r\in(1/2,1]$.

items.title: One shared face-average degree of freedom
items.statement:
Let $F$ be an interior facet of a finite matching mesh and let $\phi_F$ be
the global CR basis function indexed by $F$. It has face mean one on $F$ and
zero on every other facet. It is supported only on the two cells incident to
$F$.
